sentences.chinese: 太子前衛率徐邈議：「《喪服傳》稱與尊者為體，則不服其私親。
sentences.literal: Former crown-prince guard commander Xu Miao debated: "The Mourning Garments Commentary states that when one forms one body with the honored person, then one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.
sentences.idiomatic: Xu Miao, lately commander of the crown prince's guard, cited the Mourning Garments subcommentary: whoever is ritually one with a superior does not observe mourning for a private parent.

sentences.chinese: 又，君父所不服，子亦不敢服。
sentences.literal: Moreover, what lord and father does not wear, the son likewise dare not wear.
sentences.idiomatic: Moreover, a son may not wear mourning that his sovereign father foregoes.

sentences.chinese: 故王公妾子服其所生母練冠麻衣，既葬而除，非五服之常，則謂之無服。
sentences.literal: Therefore royal lords' sons by concubines wear for their birth mothers lien cap and hemp cloth—once buried then remove—not among the five garments' constant norms—then it is called having no garment.
sentences.idiomatic: Hence princes' sons by concubines wear only a plain lien cap and hemp until burial, then lay them aside—outside the five canonical grades—ritually counted as "no mourning."

sentences.chinese: 」從之。
sentences.literal: " This was followed.
sentences.idiomatic: " The court accepted his reading.

sentences.chinese: ，孝武帝崩，孝武太后制三年之服。
sentences.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Emperor Xiaowu died—Empress Dowager Xiaowu regulated three years' garments.
sentences.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Empress Dowager Xiaowu ordered full three-year mourning.

sentences.chinese: 惠帝三月，皇太孫尚薨。
sentences.literal: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, the imperial grandson-heir Shang died.
sentences.idiomatic: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, Sima Shang, heir as imperial grandson, died.

sentences.chinese: 有司奏，御服齊衰期。
sentences.literal: The offices memorialized that the sovereign should wear qi-cui for one full year (qi).
sentences.idiomatic: The authorities asked that the emperor observe qi-cui mourning for the standard one-year term.

sentences.chinese: 詔下通議。
sentences.literal: An edict ordered general court deliberation.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne sent down an edict for the whole bureaucracy to debate the matter.

sentences.chinese: 散騎常侍謝衡以為：「諸侯之太子，誓與未誓，尊卑體殊。
sentences.literal: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.
sentences.idiomatic: Xie Heng, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, argued that for a feudal heir's ritual standing, whether or not he had undergone the sworn presentation rite made a real difference in rank and ritual "one body."

sentences.chinese: 《喪服》云為嫡子長殤，謂未誓也，已誓則不殤也。
sentences.literal: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang.
sentences.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments canon treats mourning for an eldest legitimate son who dies in the "long shang" bracket as applying only before the sworn presentation; after that rite he is no longer classed as a shang death.

sentences.chinese: 」中書令卞粹曰：「太子始生，故已尊重，不待命誓。
sentences.literal: " Minister of the Secretariat Bian Cui said: "The heir apparent from birth is therefore already honored high—does not await mandate-swearing.
sentences.idiomatic: Bian Cui, minister of the Secretariat, answered that a crown prince is already supreme in rank from birth and does not wait upon any separate mandate or sworn presentation.

sentences.chinese: 若衡議已誓不殤，則無服之子當斬衰三年；
sentences.literal: If by Xie's debate sworn means not shang, then the son for whom there is no [shang-scale] garment ought wear zhan-cui three years;
sentences.idiomatic: If Xie's rule—sworn, therefore not shang—were accepted, any son outside the shang grades would require the mourner to wear zhan-cui for three full years;

sentences.chinese: 未誓而殤，則雖十九當大功九月。
sentences.literal: not sworn and [dies as] shang, then though age nineteen ought wear da gong nine months.
sentences.idiomatic: yet if he had not been sworn and still counted as shang, even at nineteen the prescribed grade would be only da gong for nine months.

sentences.chinese: 誓與未誓，其為升降也微；
sentences.literal: Sworn and not sworn—the rise and fall therein is slight;
sentences.idiomatic: The ritual gap between sworn and unsworn is tiny;

sentences.chinese: 斬衰與大功，其為輕重也遠。
sentences.literal: zhan-cui and da gong—the light and heavy therein is far apart.
sentences.idiomatic: but the gulf between zhan-cui and da gong is enormous.

sentences.chinese: 而今注云『諸侯不降嫡殤重』。
sentences.literal: Yet now the commentary states 'feudal lords do not lower the weight of legitimate-son shang.'
sentences.idiomatic: The gloss nonetheless says feudal lords do not mitigate mourning for a legitimate son who dies young.

sentences.chinese: 嫌于無服，以大功為重嫡之服，則雖誓，無復有三年之理明矣。
sentences.literal: Loath to [say] no garment, taking da gong as the garment weighting the legitimate heir—then though sworn, there is no longer principle for three years—this is clear.
sentences.idiomatic: To avoid calling it "no mourning," commentators assign da gong as the heavy mourning for the heir—so even after the sworn rite, three years of zhan-cui simply cannot apply. That much is plain.

sentences.chinese: 男能衛社稷，女能奉婦道，以可成之年而有已成之事，故可無殤，非孩齔之謂也。
sentences.literal: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.
sentences.idiomatic: A lad old enough to defend the altars, or a girl able to discharge a wife's duties, has crossed out of the shang brackets once capable adulthood is acknowledged—not toddlers still at breast.

sentences.chinese: 為殤後者尊之如父，猶無所加而止殤服，況以天子之尊，而為無服之殤行成人之制邪！
sentences.literal: One who succeeds a shang [decedent] honors him like a father—still adds nothing and stops at shang garment—how much more with Heaven's Son's honor to enact adult norms for a shang without garment!
sentences.idiomatic: An heir who continues a shang line honors the dead like a father yet still caps mourning at the shang grades—how then could the Son of Heaven impose full adult mourning where the canon prescribes none?

sentences.chinese: 凡諸宜重之殤，皆士大夫不加服，而令至尊獨居其重，未之前聞也。
sentences.literal: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard.
sentences.idiomatic: Every other heavy shang case lets ministers stop short of extra mourning; to load that weight solely onto the sovereign would be without precedent.

sentences.chinese: 」博士蔡克同粹。
sentences.literal: " Erudite Cai Ke agreed with Bian Cui.
sentences.idiomatic: Court erudite Cai Ke sided with Bian Cui.

sentences.chinese: 秘書監摯虞云：「太子初生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。
sentences.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, director of the palace library, said the crown prince is invested from birth with ceremonies meant for adults, so the logic of "shang" mourning drops away entirely.

sentences.chinese: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服，全非以年也。
sentences.literal: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.
sentences.idiomatic: The imperial grandson-heir likewise embodies the ruler and bears the ritual "weight"; mourning follows his station, not his calendar age.

sentences.chinese: 天子無服殤之義，絕期故也。
sentences.literal: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi).
sentences.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven never wears shang-grade mourning for kin, precisely because those relationships are ritually severed at the one-year boundary.

sentences.chinese: 」於是從之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon [the court] followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: The court adopted this view.

sentences.chinese: 魏氏故事，國有大喪，群臣凶服，以帛為綬囊，以布為劍衣。
sentences.literal: Wei-house precedent: when the state had great mourning, many ministers wore funeral dress—silk for seal-cord pouches, cloth for sword sheaths.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Wei dynasty usage, a dynastic funeral saw ministers in mourning garb with silk pouches for seal cords and cloth wrappers for swords.

sentences.chinese: 新禮，以《傳》稱「去喪無所不佩」，明在喪則無佩也，更制齊斬之喪不佩劍綬。
sentences.literal: The New Rites, because the Commentary states 'upon leaving mourning nothing is not suspended,' clarifies that in mourning there is no suspension—reformed so qi-cui and zhan-cui mourning do not suspend sword and seal cord.
sentences.idiomatic: The Jin "New Rites" cited the gloss "after mourning ends, everything may hang from the belt" to infer that during mourning nothing should hang there, and barred sword and seal cord under qi-cui and zhan-cui.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為「《周禮》武賁氏，士大夫之職也，皆以兵守王宮，國有喪故，則衰葛執戈楯守門，葬則從車而哭。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu held that "the Zhou Rites' Wu-ben guards—great officers' duty—all with arms guard the royal palace; when the state has mourning cause, then [wear] frayed robe and kudzu, grasp halberd and shield guarding gates; at burial then follow carts and wail.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu countered that the Zhou Rites' royal guardsmen were officers under arms who defended the palace; on a national bereavement they wore mourning hemp with shield and polearm at the gates and followed the hearse wailing.

sentences.chinese: 又，成王崩，太保命諸大夫以干戈內外警設。
sentences.literal: Moreover, when King Cheng died, Grand Protect ordered various great officers with shields and halberds to set inner and outer vigil.
sentences.idiomatic: When King Cheng died, the Grand Protect ordered ministers to stand watch inside and out with shields and halberds.

sentences.chinese: 明喪故之際，蓋重宿衛之防。
sentences.literal: This clarifies that at mourning's crisis one esteems night-watch defense.
sentences.idiomatic: That shows how gravely a reign treats palace security even amid mourning.

sentences.chinese: 去喪無所不佩，謂服飾之事，不謂防禦之用。
sentences.literal: 'Upon leaving mourning nothing not suspended' speaks of adornment matters—not defense uses.
sentences.idiomatic: "Nothing suspended after mourning" governs dress ornaments, not weapons of defense.

sentences.chinese: 宜定新禮布衣劍如舊，其餘如新制。
sentences.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites: cloth garment and sword as of old—the rest as new regulation.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites should keep cloth sword covers as before and leave the rest under the new rules.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: " An edict followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: An edict accepted his recommendation.

sentences.chinese: 漢魏故事，將葬，設吉凶鹵簿，皆以鼓吹。
sentences.literal: Han-Wei precedent: nearing burial, set auspicious and inauspicious halberd-escort arrays—all used drum-and-pipe.
sentences.idiomatic: Han and Wei practice paired auspicious and funeral halberd escorts at burial, both complete with military music.

sentences.chinese: 新禮以禮無吉駕導從之文，臣子不宜釋其衰麻以服玄黃，除吉駕鹵簿。
sentences.literal: The New Rites held the rites lack text for auspicious carriages with outriders—ministers and sons ought not shed their frayed hemp to wear black-and-yellow—removed auspicious-carriage halberd escort.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites argued classical texts never sanctioned festive carriages and outriders for a burial, so ministers should not strip mourning hemp for court blacks—and struck the auspicious half of the halberd escort.

sentences.chinese: 又，凶事無樂，遏密八音，除凶服之鼓吹。
sentences.literal: Moreover, inauspicious affairs have no music—suppress and silence the eight tones—removed drum-and-pipe from funeral dress [processions].
sentences.idiomatic: Funerals should silence every instrument, they added, so drum-and-pipe bands had to go from the mourning procession as well.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為：「葬有祥車曠左，則今之容車也。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Burial has auspicious cart with empty left seat—that is today's appearance cart.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu replied that the classic "auspicious cart with the left seat left empty" is the ancestor of today's display carriage.

sentences.chinese: 既葬，日中反虞，逆神而還。
sentences.literal: Once buried, at midday perform returning yu, welcome the spirit back.
sentences.idiomatic: After interment, the noon returning-yu rite escorts the spirit home again.

sentences.chinese: 《春秋傳》，鄭大夫公孫蠆卒，天子追賜大路，使以行。
sentences.literal: The Spring and Autumn Commentary: Zheng grand officer Gongsun Chai died—the Son of Heaven posthumously granted great road-chariot, ordering it used for the procession.
sentences.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition records how, when Zheng minister Gongsun Chai died, the Zhou king sent a state chariot so the cortège could ride in due splendor.

sentences.chinese: 《士喪禮》，葬有稿車乘車，以載生之服。
sentences.literal: The Gentlemen's Mourning Rites: burial has straw cart and riding cart—to carry garb [used] in life.
sentences.idiomatic: The "Gentleman's Mourning" specifies straw carts and riding carts bearing the clothes the dead wore in life.

sentences.chinese: 此皆不唯載柩，兼有吉駕之明文也。
sentences.literal: These all not only bear the coffin—together they have explicit text for auspicious carriages.
sentences.idiomatic: Those provisions plainly sanction festive vehicles alongside the bier, not coffins alone.

sentences.chinese: 既設吉駕，則宜有導從，以象平生之容，明不致死之義。
sentences.literal: Once auspicious carriages are set, then fittingly there should be outriders—to image deportment in life, clarifying the meaning of not treating [the deceased] as utterly dead.
sentences.idiomatic: Where such carriages appear, outriders belong too—the ritual echoes how the noble lived and insists he is not cast away like carrion.

sentences.chinese: 臣子衰麻不得為身而釋，以為君父則無不可。
sentences.literal: Ministers and sons in frayed hemp may not for themselves shed—for lord and father then nothing impermissible.
sentences.idiomatic: A minister may not shrug off mourning for private convenience, yet for his lord or father nothing in the canon forbids fitting splendor to the cortège.

sentences.chinese: 《顧命》之篇足以明之。
sentences.literal: The 'Charge at Gu' piece suffices to clarify this.
sentences.idiomatic: The "Charge at Gu" chapter of the Documents proves the point.

sentences.chinese: 宜定新禮設吉服導從如舊，其凶服鼓吹宜除。
sentences.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites to set auspicious-garment outriders as of old—the funeral drum-and-pipe ought be removed.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu urged restoring festive outriders under the New Rites while still banning martial music on the mourning train.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: " An edict followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.chinese: 漢魏故事，大喪及大臣之喪，執紼者輓歌。
sentences.literal: Han-Wei precedent: great mourning and great ministers' mourning—those holding tow-ropes sang dirges.
sentences.idiomatic: Han and Wei custom had catafalque bearers chant pulling-dirges at imperial funerals and at those of great ministers.

sentences.chinese: 新禮以為輓歌出於漢武帝役人之勞歌，聲哀切，遂以為送終之禮。
sentences.literal: The New Rites held dirges arose from Han Emperor Wu's corvée people's labor songs—sound mournful and piercing—thereupon taken as seeing-off-the-end rite.
sentences.idiomatic: The New Rites traced those laments to corvée labor songs under Emperor Wu—voices sharp with grief—and showed how they had hardened into funeral practice.

sentences.chinese: 雖音曲摧愴，非經典所制，違禮設銜枚之義。
sentences.literal: Though melody is crushing-grief—not fashioned by classics—contravenes the rites' meaning of mouth-plugs.
sentences.idiomatic: However wrenching the tunes, they are nowhere mandated in the classics and violate the spirit of biting wooden gag-bits to keep silence.

sentences.chinese: 方在號慕，不宜以歌為名。
sentences.literal: Just now in wailing longing—not fitting to take 'song' as name.
sentences.idiomatic: Mid-wail for the dead, nothing should parade under the label of "song."

sentences.chinese: 除，不輓歌。
sentences.literal: Removed—no dirges.
sentences.idiomatic: The reform abolished pulling-dirges altogether.

sentences.chinese: 摯虞以為：「輓歌因倡和而為摧愴之聲，銜枚所以全哀，此亦以感眾。
sentences.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued that antiphonal dirges shape communal grief, much as gag-bits enforce solemn silence—they stir the throng rather than cheapen it.

sentences.chinese: 雖非經典所載，是歷代故事。
sentences.literal: Though not carried in classics—it is successive dynasties' precedent.
sentences.idiomatic: They never appear verbatim in the canon, yet dynasty after dynasty relied on them.

sentences.chinese: 《詩》稱『君子作歌，惟以告哀』，以歌為名，亦無所嫌。
sentences.literal: The Odes state 'the gentleman makes song—only to declare grief'—to take song as name—also nothing blameworthy.
sentences.idiomatic: The Odes themselves praise the gentleman who "raises a song only to voice sorrow," so the word "song" is hardly improper.

sentences.chinese: 宜定新禮如舊。
sentences.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites as of old.
sentences.idiomatic: He asked that the New Rites reinstate the older practice.

sentences.chinese: 」詔從之。
sentences.literal: " An edict followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: The court accepted his opinion.

sentences.chinese: ，安平穆王薨，無嗣，以母弟敦上繼獻王後，移太常問應何服。
sentences.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Prince Mu of Anping died—no heir—his uterine younger brother Dun was elevated to continue Prince Xian's line—the case was referred to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials asking what mourning ought apply.
sentences.idiomatic: When Prince Mu of Anping died without issue, his full brother Sima Dun was promoted to continue Prince Xian's line; the matter went to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to settle the proper mourning grades.

sentences.chinese: 博士張靖答，宜依魯僖服閔三年例。
sentences.literal: Erudite Zhang Jing replied—it should follow Duke Xi of Lu's mourning Duke Min three-year precedent.
sentences.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Jing answered that the parallel was Duke Xi of Lu wearing three years' mourning for Duke Min.

sentences.chinese: 尚書符詰靖：「穆王不臣敦，敦不繼穆，與閔僖不同。
sentences.literal: The Secretariat issued a writ pressing Jing: "Prince Mu did not treat Dun as subject—Dun does not succeed Mu—this differs from Min and Xi.
sentences.idiomatic: The Secretariat shot back: Prince Mu never treated Dun as his subject, and Dun was not succeeding Prince Mu himself—nothing like the Duke Min and Duke Xi case.

sentences.chinese: 」孫毓、宋昌議，以穆王不之國，敦不仕諸侯，不應三年。
sentences.literal: " Sun Yu and Song Chang debated that because Prince Mu never went to his fief and Dun never served feudal lords, three years should not apply.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Yu and Song Chang countered that because Prince Mu never took up his fief and Dun had never served as a feudal officer, full three-year mourning was out of the question.

sentences.chinese: 以義處之，敦宜服本服，一期而除，主穆王喪祭三年畢，乃吉祭獻王。
sentences.literal: Judging by right principle, Dun ought wear his proper garment—remove after one full cycle (qi)—preside over Prince Mu's mourning sacrifices completing three years—then perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian.
sentences.idiomatic: On principle, Dun should wear only his own proper grade—doffing it after the one-year term—yet still oversee Prince Mu's mortuary rites through three years before he may offer auspicious sacrifices to Prince Xian.

sentences.chinese: 毓云：「《禮》，君之子孫所以臣諸兄者，以臨國故也。
sentences.literal: Sun Yu said: "By the Rites, why lord's descendants treat elder brothers as lord—because they face the state.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Yu cited the canon: princes' sons honor elder brothers as lords only when they actually rule a state.

sentences.chinese: 《禮》又與諸侯為兄弟服斬者，謂鄰國之臣於鄰國之君，有猶君之義故也。
sentences.literal: The Rites moreover [say] wearing zhan-cui for feudal-lord brothers means neighboring state's ministers toward neighboring state's lord—because there is quasi-lord meaning.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhan-cui for a brother who is another state's ruler applies only where ministers owe their neighbor's prince something like fealty.

sentences.chinese: 今穆王既不之國，不臣兄弟，敦不仕諸侯，無鄰臣之義，異于閔僖，如符旨也。
sentences.literal: Now Prince Mu neither went to state nor treated brothers as subjects—Dun never served feudal lords—no neighboring-minister meaning—differs from Min and Xi—as the writ's intent [states].
sentences.idiomatic: Here Prince Mu never took his throne in the fief, never treated brothers as vassals, and Dun was no feudal minister—so none of the "neighbor's minister" logic applies, exactly as the Secretariat argued.

sentences.chinese: 但喪無主，敦既奉詔紹國，受重主喪，典其祭祀。
sentences.literal: But mourning lacked a master—Dun having received edict to continue the state—received weight and presided mourning—administers its sacrifices.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet the bereavement had no ritual head; Dun, ordered to continue the line, carries the "weight" of heirship, directs the funeral, and manages the offerings.

sentences.chinese: 『大功者主人之喪，有三年者則必為之再祭』。
sentences.literal: 'For da gong [mourning] the master's mourning—if there is one with three years then must perform for him twice the sacrifice.'
sentences.idiomatic: "When the chief mourner wears da gong but someone else in the household still owes three full years, he must conduct both intermediate auspicious rites for them."

sentences.chinese: 鄭氏《注》云，『謂死者之從父昆弟來為喪主也。
sentences.literal: Zheng's Commentary states: '[This] means the deceased's father's brothers' sons who come as mourning master.
sentences.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses this as paternal cousins who arrive to act as funeral master.

sentences.chinese: 」有三年者，謂妻若子幼少也』。
sentences.literal: [Text joins prior quotation;] 'those who have three years' refers to wife or young children (close of Zheng Xuan gloss).
sentences.idiomatic: Zheng finishes the gloss: the survivors who still owe three years are the widow or very young children.

sentences.chinese: 『再祭，謂大小祥也』。
sentences.literal: 'Twice sacrifice means great and small xiang.'
sentences.idiomatic: "The two offerings are the great and small xiang rites."

sentences.chinese: 穆妃及國臣於禮皆當三年，此為有三年者，敦當為之主大小兩祥祭也。
sentences.literal: Prince Mu's consort and state ministers by rites all ought three years—these are those with three years—Dun ought for them preside both great- and small-xiang sacrifices.
sentences.idiomatic: Prince Mu's consort and his household ministers each owe three years of mourning; they are the "three-year" parties for whom Dun must preside over both xiang ceremonies.

sentences.chinese: 且哀樂不相雜，吉凶不相干。
sentences.literal: Moreover grief and joy do not mix—inauspicious and auspicious do not cross.
sentences.idiomatic: Moreover grief must not mingle with celebration, nor mourning with felicity.

sentences.chinese: 凶服在宮，哭泣未絕。
sentences.literal: Funeral dress in the palace—wailing not ceased.
sentences.idiomatic: Funeral weeds still fill the palace and wails have not fallen silent.

sentences.chinese: 敦遽主穆王之喪，而國制未除，則不得以己本親服除而吉祭獻王也。」
sentences.literal: Dun hastily presides Prince Mu's mourning—yet state regulation not removed—then may not with his own kin garment removed perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian."
sentences.idiomatic: While Dun is abruptly directing Prince Mu's obsequies and the prescribed mourning is unfinished, he cannot shed mourning for his natural kin and turn to auspicious rites for Prince Xian."

sentences.chinese: ，陳留國上，燕公是王之父，王出奉明帝祀，今于王為從父，有司奏應服期，不以親疏尊卑為降。
sentences.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chenliu state reported—the Duke of Yan is the king's father—the king went out to serve Emperor Ming's sacrifices—now toward the king [the duke] is congfu kin—the offices memorialized [the duke] ought wear qi (one full cycle) mourning—not lowering by kin distance or honor base.
sentences.idiomatic: Chenliu memorialized that the Duke of Yan was the king's natural father; once the king had been given to continue Emperor Ming's line, the duke counted only as a congfu relative. Officials proposed qi-grade mourning with no reduction for intimacy or rank.

sentences.chinese: 詔曰：「王奉魏氏，所承者重，不得服其私親。
sentences.literal: Edict stated: "The king carries Wei house—the inheritance is weighty—may not wear for private kin.
sentences.idiomatic: An edict refused: "The king upholds Wei ancestry under grave obligation; he cannot observe mourning for a private parent."

sentences.chinese: 」穆帝時，東海國言，哀王薨逾年，嗣王乃來繼，不復追服，群臣皆已反吉，國妃亦宜同除。
sentences.literal: " Under Emperor Mu, Donghai state reported—King Ai died over a year—then the successor king came to continue—did not retroactively wear mourning—all ministers already returned auspicious—the state's royal consort likewise ought remove together.
sentences.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Mu, Donghai argued that King Ai had been dead more than a year before the heir arrived, so no retroactive mourning was worn; ministers had all returned to felicity garb, and the princess-consort should shed weeds as well.

sentences.chinese: 詔曰：「朝廷所以從權制者，以王事奪之，非為變禮也。
sentences.literal: Edict stated: "Why the court followed expedient regulation—because royal affairs seized them—not to alter the rites.
sentences.idiomatic: The edict answered: "We shortened mourning only because state business overrode private duty—not to rewrite the canon."

sentences.chinese: 婦人傳重義大，若從權制，義將安托！
sentences.literal: Women's transmitting weight—right meaning is great—if following expedient regulation—where will right rest!
sentences.idiomatic: Women who bear the ritual "weight" of heirship hold immense obligation—if we subject them to the same expedient, where does principle find footing?

sentences.chinese: 」於是國妃終三年之禮。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon the state's royal consort completed three years' rites.
sentences.idiomatic: The princess-consort therefore observed the full three-year mourning.

sentences.chinese: 孫盛以為：「廢三年之禮，開偷薄之源，漢魏失之大者也。
sentences.literal: Sun Sheng held: "Abolishing three years' rites—opens source of stingy thinness—Han-Wei's great failure.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Sheng thought waiving three-year mourning opened the floodgates to meanness—that was Han and Wei's gravest ritual lapse.

sentences.chinese: 今若以大夫宜奪以王事。
sentences.literal: Now if holding great officers ought be seized by royal affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: If we allow that grandees may be yanked from mourning by state business,

sentences.chinese: 婦人可終本服，是吉凶之儀雜陳于宮寢，彩素之制乖異於內外，無乃情禮俱違，哀樂失所乎！」
sentences.literal: women may complete proper garment—is this not auspicious and inauspicious observances mixed in palace chambers—bright and plain regulations contrary inner and outer—surely emotion and rites both violated—grief and joy lose their place!"
sentences.idiomatic: yet women finish full mourning for kin, would we not parade mourning and felicity through the same inner chambers, clash bright dress with hemp inside and out, and undo both feeling and ritual until grief and joy lose their proper seats?"

sentences.chinese: ，太常車胤上言：「謹案《喪服禮經》，庶子為母緦麻三月。
sentences.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chamberlain for Ceremonials Che Yin submitted: "Respectfully reviewing the Mourning Garments ritual classic—a son by concubine for mother [wears] si (fine hemp) three months.
sentences.idiomatic: Che Yin, chamberlain for ceremonials, cited the Mourning Garments classic: a concubine's son owes his mother only three months in si-grade hemp.

sentences.chinese: 《傳》曰：『何以緦麻？
sentences.literal: The Commentary states: 'Why si?
sentences.idiomatic: The subcommentary asks why si applies.

sentences.chinese: 以尊者為體，不敢服其私親也。
sentences.literal: Because one forms body with the honored—dare not wear for private kin.
sentences.idiomatic: Because the heir is ritually one with his exalted father, he cannot wear heavy mourning for a private parent.

sentences.chinese: 』此《經》《傳》之明文，聖賢之格言。
sentences.literal: ' This is classic and commentary's clear text—sages' model words.
sentences.idiomatic: That pairing of text and gloss is explicit scripture—language the sages meant as normative.

sentences.chinese: 而自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後，各肆私情，服其庶母，同之於嫡。
sentences.literal: Yet from recently enfeoffed dukes and marquises down to ministers—sons by concubine who became heirs—each indulged private feeling—wore mourning for concubine-mothers—equating to legitimate mother.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet lately every enfeoffed noble down to senior ministers, once a concubine's son succeeded, indulged private affection and mourned a concubine-mother like a legal parent.

sentences.chinese: 此末俗之弊，溺情傷教，縱而不革，則流遁忘返矣。
sentences.literal: This is late custom's harm—drowning feeling injures teaching—if indulged and not reformed—then drift astray unable return.
sentences.idiomatic: That late-born abuse drowns sentiment and wounds instruction; left unchecked, custom slides past recall.

sentences.chinese: 且夫尊尊親親，雖禮之大本，然厭親于尊，由來尚矣。
sentences.literal: Moreover honoring honor and kinning kin—though rites' great root—yet subordinating kin to honor—from antiquity esteemed.
sentences.idiomatic: Honoring superiors and cherishing kin are the roots of ritual, yet subordinating private kin to public rank has been honored since high antiquity.

sentences.chinese: 《禮記》曰，『為父後，出母無服也者，不祭故也』。
sentences.literal: The Record of Rites states: 'Acting as father's heir—divorced mother no garment—because [one does] not sacrifice [to her] thereby.'
sentences.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says an heir to his father wears nothing for a divorced mother because he no longer sacrifices to her.

sentences.chinese: 又，禮，天子父母之喪，未葬，越紼而祭天地社稷。
sentences.literal: Moreover, by rites—Son of Heaven's father-mother mourning—not yet buried—step over rope-coffin and sacrifice to Heaven Earth soil and grain.
sentences.idiomatic: Again, the Son of Heaven may vault the burial cord before interment and still offer to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.chinese: 斯皆崇嚴至敬，不敢以私廢尊也。
sentences.literal: These all exalt stern utmost reverence—dare not with private discard honor.
sentences.idiomatic: Such acts exalt awe before public cult—never letting private grief scrap obligations to the supreme powers.

sentences.chinese: 今身承祖宗之重，而以庶母之私，廢烝嘗之事。
sentences.literal: Now personally bearing ancestors' weight—yet with concubine-mother's private—abolish zheng-offering and chang-offering affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: Today heirs shoulder ancestral temples yet scrap winter and autumn offerings for a concubine mother's sake.

sentences.chinese: 五廟闕祀，由一妾之終，求之情禮，失莫大焉。
sentences.literal: Five temples lack sacrifice—because one concubine's end—seek in emotion and rites—failure none greater.
sentences.idiomatic: Five shrines miss sacrifice because one concubine died—by any measure of feeling or ritual, the harm could hardly be worse.

sentences.chinese: 舉世皆然，莫之裁貶。
sentences.literal: Whole age thus—none trims or faults it.
sentences.idiomatic: Everyone does it; nobody reins it in.

sentences.chinese: 就心不同，而事不敢異。
sentences.literal: In heart disagree—but in deed dare not differ.
sentences.idiomatic: Men may dissent inwardly yet dare not break step in public.

sentences.chinese: 故正禮遂穨，而習非成俗。
sentences.literal: Hence correct rites thus crumble—and habit wrong becomes custom.
sentences.idiomatic: Thus orthodox ritual collapses while repeated error hardens into custom.

sentences.chinese: 此《國風》所以思古，《小雅》所以悲歎。
sentences.literal: This is why Airs of the States longs for antiquity—why Lesser Odes laments.
sentences.idiomatic: This is why the Airs of the States sigh for ancient ways and the Lesser Odes pour out their grief.

sentences.chinese: 當今九服漸甯，王化惟新，誠宜崇明禮訓，以一風俗。
sentences.literal: Now the nine domains gradually pacified—kingly transformation anew—truly fitting exalt bright ritual instruction—to unify customs.
sentences.idiomatic: With the nine circuits calming and royal influence renewing, it is time to lift bright ritual teaching and knit the realm into one custom.

sentences.chinese: 請臺省考修經典，式明王度。
sentences.literal: Request terrace and provincial offices examine and revise classics—to pattern-clarify kingly measure.
sentences.idiomatic: He asked the central departments to collate the classics and codify them so the kingly norm shines clear.
